clue.text: Sweet, intoxicating drink? Try fizzy cola first

indicators.note: tells the solver to put the rearranged drink at the front, ahead of the other piece
a fizzy drink is agitated and bubbling, so the letters of the drink named next are stirred up

parts.note: the soft drink, as written, before rearranging
to have a pop at something is to try it

explanation.surface: A tasting note for a sugary boozy drink, suggesting you start with a fizzy cola.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the definition: an alcopop is sweet and alcoholic. 'Try' is the instruction-looking word that actually supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sugary ready-mixed alcoholic beverage sold like a soft drink.

clue.text: One task left unfinished by new presenter

indicators.note: a job left unfinished lacks its final step, so the word loses its last letter
by means next to, so the abbreviation sits alongside the other pieces

parts.note: a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: Someone new to presenting leaves a job half done.
explanation.walkthrough: The N slots between the A and the clipped CHORE, which is where 'by' lets it sit.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main presenter who links a news or television programme.

clue.text: Bloke Tess outwardly desires

parts.note: cove is old slang for a man or fellow

indicators.note: outwardly points to the outside of the name, so only its first and last letters count

parts.note: the two outside letters of the name

explanation.surface: A man finds Tess attractive, at least on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to long for something, especially something belonging to another, so desires is a synonym.

clue.text: Brunel thus does about-turn in well-mannered debate about government, say

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the word for well-mannered, splitting it open

parts.note: Brunel is the setter, who refers to himself as I

indicators.note: an about-turn faces the other way, so the Latin word is read from the end back

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quoted error

explanation.surface: The setter changes his mind in a courteous discussion about government.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for I, as 'this setter' or 'me' often does. POLIT and E wrap round I plus CIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To politicise is to talk or argue about political matters, which is what discussing government is, hence 'say'.

clue.text: It has to be paid, Katie

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cost of something
second meaning: surname of Katie, a British glamour model and media personality

explanation.surface: Someone is told a bill is due, addressed to Katie.
explanation.walkthrough: Katie Price is a well-known British model and reality-television figure, so her first name points to the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A price is the sum charged for something, and Katie Price is a famous British celebrity.

clue.text: Small cars no-go area encompassing eastern city

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the compass point is held inside what comes before it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: no means without, so the following short word is taken out of the vehicles

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to remove
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A city bans little cars from a zone in its eastern district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-go area' looks like one phrase but splits three ways: no, go, and area. Railway cars are a common crossword sense of 'cars'. Swansea is a city in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in Wales, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Makes neater by switching higher trees around

indicators.note: switching round swaps the order, so the front piece is moved to the end
around reinforces the turning about, the leading piece going round to the back

explanation.surface: Tidying a garden by rearranging the taller trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce up is to tidy or smarten, making something neater.

clue.text: The last word in Puma menswear

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the brand and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A sportswear brand's men's range is declared the height of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last word' sounds like praise for the clothes, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the close of a prayer, literally the final utterance.

clue.text: Old heartthrob Distel embraces one boarding swanky car — spicy stuff!

indicators.note: someone boarding a vehicle gets inside it, so the numeral goes into the car

parts.note: Sacha Distel was a French crooner and sixties pin-up

indicators.note: an embrace wraps round, so the singer's name holds the car with its passenger

parts.note: RR is short for Rolls-Royce, the classic posh car

explanation.surface: A former French heartthrob climbs into a luxury car, then the exclamation about something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the numeral boards the car, and the singer's name embraces the loaded car just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sriracha is a hot chilli sauce from Thailand, a condiment described loosely as spicy stuff.

clue.text: Opening time to be put back across country, Tory leader admitted

indicators.note: across means spread over the other pieces, so the turned word straddles them
putting the clock back runs time the other way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so this letter also goes inside the turned word
a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of the party is used

explanation.surface: Pub opening hours are pushed back nationally, as admitted by a Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening time' looks like pub hours, but only 'Opening' is the definition; 'time' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a hole or gap, the same thing as an opening.

clue.text: Faceless ones traditionally invoked by polite ceremony

parts.note: a service is a religious ceremony

explanation.surface: Faceless officials are summoned through a courteous ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: Politicians and the press traditionally blame 'faceless bureaucrats', the anonymous officials of government departments.
explanation.definitionFit: The civil service is the body of anonymous government officials often called faceless bureaucrats.

clue.text: Old tribesman's alternative realities

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different arrangement, so the letters are shuffled into another order

explanation.surface: An ancient tribesman is said to live in alternative realities.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite was a member of one of the ancient Hebrew tribes descended from Jacob.

clue.text: Extend reorganisation of the Court's time

indicators.note: reorganising something rearranges it, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A reorganisation of the court's sitting hours is used to give it more time.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstretch is to stretch out or reach further, so it is a synonym of extend.

clue.text: Split bit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to separate, as people do
second meaning: a portion or piece

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it sounds like a small piece of something broken; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to separate or divide, and a part is one portion of a whole.

clue.text: Manager in 'Association' shattered old Cup record

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into fragments, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A football Association boss breaks a long-standing cup record.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'Association' explains the prefix: a co- producer manages a film or show in association with another.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-producer jointly manages the production of a film or show alongside a partner.

clue.text: Companion attending king is peerless — the woman's a saint

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A royal attendant is unrivalled, and the woman in the story is a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the post-nominal for the Order of the Companions of Honour, a British honour; 'attending' just places it beside the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher is the patron saint of travellers, so the name is an example of a saint.

clue.text: Looter hid abandoned gemstone

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A thief stashed a precious stone and then left it behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as the looter deserting the stone, but it signals the letters running wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodolite is a rose-red or purple variety of garnet used as a gem.

clue.text: A Microsoft mogul overcomes computing worries

indicators.note: in a down clue overcomes reads as goes over and round, so the tycoon's name wraps the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A software billionaire beats his worries about computers.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate someone is to stir up anxiety, so it means worries as a transitive verb.

clue.text: Better to lift second appliance inside cupboard, possibly

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the letter higher, so it is dropped back in nearer the top
lifting something takes it up out of its place, so this letter is removed from where it sits

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A gambler hoists his second appliance into a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is not 'superior' but one who bets. In a down entry, lifting the S moves it two places nearer the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter records household gas use and is often housed in a cupboard, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Initially guys rather like, perhaps, girl in M&S jumper

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words that come next

parts.note: as means in the way of, like
a woman in Marks and Spencer may well be a shopper

explanation.surface: Blokes apparently fancy a girl wearing a Marks and Spencer jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks and Spencer, a British high-street store; jumper is British for sweater, but here it is the insect that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasshopper is an insect famous for leaping, so it is literally a jumper.

clue.text: I must replace last of cycling apparel

indicators.note: replace the final letter means the closing letter of the word is swapped out for the one named

explanation.surface: Someone insists on swapping out the last of their cycling gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The G of BIKING is swapped for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit, an item of clothing, which apparel covers.

clue.text: Having gone outside, Girl Guides knocked back drink

indicators.note: knocked back means sent back, so the whole combination runs the other way
the word for having left goes round the outside of the abbreviation

explanation.surface: After leaving the building, Girl Guides downed a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, which suits the surface, but it signals the reversal. Girl Guides are the British equivalent of Girl Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a drink of beaten eggs, milk and often spirits, popular at Christmas.

clue.text: Terrible gutless politician — her stay in office will be brief

definitions.text: her stay in office will be brief

indicators.note: without guts means with the insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cowardly, useless politician will not last long in government.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a jab at a short-lived minister, but 'office' is a workplace and a temp works there briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp is a temporary office worker, employed for a short period only.

clue.text: Maybe sinking ship off port at start of enemy action

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
start points to the opening letter of the next word only

parts.note: doing is an act or action

explanation.surface: A vessel leaves harbour just as hostilities begin, and may be sunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' tells you sinking a ship is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpedoing is attacking with an underwater missile, one way of sinking a vessel.

clue.text: Head north in flat-bottomed vessel

parts.note: pate is the top of the head

explanation.surface: Steering a flat boat towards the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A paten is the shallow plate used for the bread at the Eucharist, a flat receptacle.

clue.text: Fairy queen overwhelms Athenian character's heart

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to flood in, so the royal abbreviation pours into the middle of the letter
the heart is the middle, which is where the royal abbreviation lands

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A fairy queen's power moves a Greek to the core.
explanation.walkthrough: An Athenian character is a Greek letter, not a person in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or good spirit in Persian mythology, known to crossword solvers.

clue.text: Parties essentially bother child: it's rejecting all outsiders, fully

indicators.note: the essence is the core, so only the central letter of the word counts

parts.note: the central letter of the seven

indicators.note: throwing out every outer letter leaves just the insides of each word

parts.note: without its first and last letters
without its first and last letters
without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A child bothers the party-goers by refusing to let strangers join.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' loses its I and S, leaving only the T.
explanation.definitionFit: To the hilt means completely, as a blade driven in up to its handle.

clue.text: It may commemorate dog

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pile of stones raised as a memorial
second meaning: a small Scottish terrier

explanation.surface: A dog might be honoured with a memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a heap of stones set up as a memorial, and also a breed of small terrier.

clue.text: See 9
Dash back, Carol — it's a sister's job

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the word for dash from right to left

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: Someone tells Carol to hurry back, since her sister needs her to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is the verb; a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursing is the profession of a nurse, and in Britain a senior ward nurse is called a sister.
